fixtures.label: Two orders at one address — both directions, crew work
fixtures.description:
The family's FIRST fixture, and the case it exists for: a CROSS-ORDER sheet at ONE address in BOTH directions. Address `destination:x07P9fuCbGctZmB4zqhg:crew:both` — what `/pick-sheet` composes for a destination bucket, whose gate DEFAULTS to `crew`. Re-captured 2026-09-09.

Six jobs; the first three separate this family from `packing-list`.

1. THE NULL LEG — "Both directions", the arm `packing-list.eta` REFUSES: it accompanies ONE movement, and rendering both doubles every rental line.
2. TWO BUCKET COLUMNS CARRYING VALUES — one column holding everything cannot show the seven-way partition.
3. THE GATE LINE — "Crew work"; both legs are ours to deliver and collect. `packing-list` prints no gate.
4. BOTH BANNER LEVELS, each on its own count: two orders and two differently-named legs at one address, under a scope line naming the ADDRESS.
5. THE BLANK-CELL EXPLANATION, both shapes. A booking is aggregate per (order, product, destination), so products repeat across legs and components across the two Pop Up Tents. One occurrence carries the numbers, the rest read "counted under …". The naive `bookings.find(...)` renders identically and states one quantity twice.
6. SERVICE ROWS with no booking — blank cells and a Total, still rows.

⭐ ONE organization, so the letterhead names it; the shared-stage arm where it must NOT (`3100 W Fillmore St`) is covered by nothing.

⭐ THE FOUR-ADDRESSES-FOR-ONE-PLACE ARTIFACT IS GONE. `applyPii` used to seed on field PATH, so `delivery.address` and `collection.address` of one `destinations/{uid}` drew different fakes — 6 of 6 same-uid pairs in this repo. core#91 seeds on the VALUE's identity, so one address is one street across the document. This golden is where that is visible.

⚠️ `scope.name` holds `destination.address.full` verbatim and is masked as an address, not as a company — `DISCRIMINANT_CATEGORY` routes it on the sibling `kind`.

⚠️ No serialized row: the Stock column is OFF on both fixtures.

fixtures.label: A line in two states at once — one order, both directions
fixtures.description:
The SPLIT BREAKDOWN — one line holding units in two custody states at once — the reason the seven columns exist. `order:V3hl7IoFE51tElz7c4fr:all:both` is the address `FulfillmentDetail`'s menu composes — the per-order printable form of that screen. Prod order 1012, one leg at our counter, 108 units, 25 rows.

⚠️ The plan behind this family recorded that NO prod or dev booking had a split, from 80 sampled. Sampling artifact: over all 7,123 dev bookings SIX do, and this is one, verified on prod. Do not re-derive the "hand-build it" conclusion.

Five jobs, none reachable from its sibling.

1. THE SPLIT — Short Director Chair, booking quantity 3, `reserved: 2` beside `out: 1`. Two populated cells on ONE row, with a Total read off the BOOKING rather than summed from them, so a partition that disagrees with its own total surfaces here.
2. ITS OWNER, on the same booking. That chair appears TWICE — under `Wardrobe` at depth 4 and under `Hair & Makeup` at depth 3 — so one occurrence prints the split and a Total of 3 on a line whose own quantity is 1, and the other prints "counted under Hair & Makeup" with blank cells. Both halves of `owner_path`, one product, one page.
3. THE `order` SCOPE — the degenerate one (api-cloudrun#821), whose scope line reads "for" rather than "everything open at"; `resolveOrderScope` had no route until `GET /pick-sheets`.
4. A SINGLE-ORDER SHEET — `showOrderBanner` and `showDestinationBanners` are both FALSE, so #details prints `#1012` where the sibling prints a count. That cell is the only place a single-order sheet names its order.
5. TWO KIT PARENTS WITH NO BOOKING — `Pipe & Drape (2 Rooms)` and `Combo Hangers (Set of 30)` are `stock_method: none`, so they render blank while their components carry the units. Same blank cells as the sibling's service rows, different cause, neither explained.

⚠️ Gate `all`, so no gate line — the sibling holds that arm. ⚠️ Pickup and Return read as two addresses; it is ONE warehouse — see the sibling.
